headline: Chief Justice Koome Reports Reduction In Judiciary Case Backlog
seoTitle: Chief Justice Koome Reports Reduction In Judiciary Backlog
metaDescription: Chief Justice Martha Koome reports a 2.5 per cent reduction in Kenya's judiciary case backlog, citing improved efficiency and systemic enhancements.
aiSummaryBullets: Chief Justice Martha Koome announced a 2.5 per cent decrease in the judiciary case backlog.
The decline is attributed to enhanced institutional efficiency and judicial system improvements.
The judiciary processed over 15,000 cases involving children, including custody matters.
aiContextParagraph: Chief Justice Martha Koome recently released performance reports highlighting recent developments within the Kenyan judiciary. According to official data, the judiciary has successfully cleared more cases than were filed for the second consecutive year, resulting in a 2.5 per cent reduction in the total case backlog. The Chief Justice attributed these gains to ongoing efforts aimed at strengthening institutional systems and increasing access to justice across the country. Additionally, the reports provided insights into specific areas of legal administration, noting that courts handled over 15,000 cases related to children, with approximately 93 per cent involving children in contact with the law or custody disputes. Despite these operational improvements, the Chief Justice also highlighted challenges related to funding gaps and reaffirmed the judiciary's commitment to eliminating bribery and ensuring transparency in all legal proceedings.
whyItIsViral: The report gained traction following coverage by two independent media outlets highlighting institutional progress and administrative data.
